title: Bind media data and UUIDs to surviving rendered order, not original message order
applies_when: A multimodal prompt encoder merges, sorts or drops messages while a separate parser collects images and cache UUIDs in input order; DeepSeek V4.1 tool-result ordering and discarded developer images are concrete examples.
lesson: Treat prompt text, media payloads and media UUIDs as one correspondence invariant. Assign image indices before preprocessing, carry them through message/block transforms, then collect only surviving indices in final rendering order and apply that selection to both data and UUID lists. Matching placeholder counts alone misses swaps; checking text alone misses extra or misbound images. Test reversed tool-result order, complete image removal, and a dropped image preceding a retained image. Exercise sync and async parsing with distinguishable image contents and UUIDs, and check that caller-owned inputs were not changed. Use the actual parser/tracker where feasible; model-metadata fixtures do not constitute real processor or serving validation.
avoid_when: Do not apply a source-image permutation to expanded crops, embeddings, video frames or another modality without proving their indexing contract. Deduplication, cache hits and duplicated references may require a different correspondence representation. Tests of two paths sharing one rendering helper can miss a common error, so include independent payload/UUID expectations. Existing merged or open repairs remain their authors' work; independent verification is not a new discovery or reason for a competing PR. Component agreement does not prove correct model outputs or whole-server compatibility.

evidence.note: Merged PR60792 applies one rendered image-order selection to both media data and UUIDs, removing the image entry when no images survive. Source mechanism, not our contribution or full-model qualification.
Source indices accompany merged user/tool blocks and are gathered during final rendering after message preprocessing, rather than inferred solely from original input order.

The public upstream tests distinguish image pixels and UUIDs in reordered tool results and exercise developer-image removal through both sync and async paths. Their fixture replaces model metadata/processor lookup; it does not load a real vision model.
